Actually in dart test output, an unhandled exception in the CLI subprocess wouldn't print that way; this looks like an unhandled async error in the test process itself. Actually — in CI this shard runs with FA_BIN=AOT binary; the CLI subprocess's unhandled exceptions are printed to its stderr, and the harness may surface stderr as a test failure. The two-line trace `HttpException ... dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage` is exactly what a Dart AOT binary prints for an unhandled async error (AOT stacks are often truncated to one frame). So: the CLI process itself hit an unhandled HttpException — an LLM client request in the CLI (or a background subagent turn in the CLI) got "Connection closed while receiving data" from the mock server, and it was UNHANDLED, crashing/failing the test.

  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1522: the publish dry-run rehearses the tag-stamped stage —
          # tag math needs the full tag graph (blobless per gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # gh-1522: the dry-run now rehearses the REAL publish payload — the
      # staged tree stamped with the NEXT tag version — so a stamp failure
      # (placeholder leak, changelog-section generation, staged-version
      # desync) surfaces nightly, not at tag time. Publish-blocking problems
      # (undeclared lib/ imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface
      # only in the tag-time publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared
      # package:cryptography import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags.
      # --ignore-warnings: the two known layout warnings (gitignored
      # install_local.sh, docs/ naming) must not redden the nightly, while
      # validation ERRORS — "does not have X in the dependencies section of
      # pubspec.yaml" — still fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a
      # publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated
      # metadata reads, so resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the
      # publish job); --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run on the staged tree (gh-1522)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the publish of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage "$next"
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub get && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): integration-tagged jsr
      # delegate suites feed the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet AND must
      # reach this unit-side lcov (the 80% ratchet + CRAP below read it) —
      # same rationale as scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        run: dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh. Bounded: a
          # floating >= would auto-adopt 0.11.0+ with no repo change.
          # gh-1106: ceiling bumped to 0.12.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml
          # duplication block now uses 0.11.0-only keys.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

  # PTY/terminal integration suites (issue #177 follow-up): mock-endpoint
  # tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests self-skip

commit d1b54ef01aaf485acc18c753051db43e3ddad645
Author: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit <vabhzw17eg2qu4m9@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Oct 10 15:41:43 2026 +0300

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

  "description": "## Owner directive

Separate card from #1537. Once #1537 makes the SM pre-merge validation the single test gate, the nightly workflow must stop re-running anything that gate already covers. Nightly keeps only what belongs there by nature:

- **Builds** (all store/desktop targets, as today).

This leg pays for itself: it caught the #1510 TUI wrap regression that unit tests could not see.

Everything else that nightly currently re-runs (unit shards, analyze, coverage, duplication/CRAP gates — audit the actual nightly workflow legs) gets REMOVED as duplication of the pre-merge gate.

## Acceptance

1. Audit nightly workflow legs; classify each as {duplicates pre-merge gate} vs {nightly-native: builds, integration tests}; the issue body lists the classification.
2. Remove the duplicating legs; keep builds + integration-only. Nightly wall time must measurably drop (note before/after in the PR).
3. Integration leg stays red-visible: its failures keep filing flake/red issues via the intake (retargeted per #1537 if needed).
4. Docs updated (AGENTS.md quality gates / docs/) to state: unit+coverage+static = pre-merge only; integration+builds = nightly.
5. If the team later wants nightly fully testless, integration tests move to on-demand/pre-release — explicitly OUT of scope here.

Refs: #1537 (retire post-merge main CI — the pre-merge gate becomes the single test gate), #1510 (proof the integration leg earns its keep).

  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1522: the publish dry-run rehearses the tag-stamped stage —
          # tag math needs the full tag graph (blobless per gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # gh-1522: the dry-run now rehearses the REAL publish payload — the
      # staged tree stamped with the NEXT tag version — so a stamp failure
      # (placeholder leak, changelog-section generation, staged-version
      # desync) surfaces nightly, not at tag time. Publish-blocking problems
      # (undeclared lib/ imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface
      # only in the tag-time publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared
      # package:cryptography import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags.
      # --ignore-warnings: the two known layout warnings (gitignored
      # install_local.sh, docs/ naming) must not redden the nightly, while
      # validation ERRORS — "does not have X in the dependencies section of
      # pubspec.yaml" — still fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a
      # publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated
      # metadata reads, so resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the
      # publish job); --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run on the staged tree (gh-1522)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the publish of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage "$next"
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub get && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): integration-tagged jsr
      # delegate suites feed the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet AND must
      # reach this unit-side lcov (the 80% ratchet + CRAP below read it) —
      # same rationale as scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        run: dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh. Bounded: a
          # floating >= would auto-adopt 0.11.0+ with no repo change.
          # gh-1106: ceiling bumped to 0.12.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml
          # duplication block now uses 0.11.0-only keys.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true

          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:

          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;

    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —

  full-quality:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1522: the publish dry-run rehearses the tag-stamped stage —
          # tag math needs the full tag graph (blobless per gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # gh-1522: the dry-run now rehearses the REAL publish payload — the
      # staged tree stamped with the NEXT tag version — so a stamp failure
      # (placeholder leak, changelog-section generation, staged-version
      # desync) surfaces nightly, not at tag time. Publish-blocking problems
      # (undeclared lib/ imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface
      # only in the tag-time publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared
      # package:cryptography import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags.
      # --ignore-warnings: the two known layout warnings (gitignored
      # install_local.sh, docs/ naming) must not redden the nightly, while
      # validation ERRORS — "does not have X in the dependencies section of
      # pubspec.yaml" — still fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a
      # publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated
      # metadata reads, so resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the
      # publish job); --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run on the staged tree (gh-1522)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the publish of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/publish-stage "$next"
          (cd /tmp/publish-stage && dart pub get && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-

Author: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit <vabhzw17eg2qu4m9@gmail.com>

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

The test failed with `HttpException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri = /v1/chat/completions`. Since the failure surfaces as the test failing with that exception, it likely propagated through the test zone.

Where does this come from? The mock server (package:fa_llm_mock) serves the parent + child turns. The error "Connection closed while receiving data" means: client (the CLI's http client, or the harness's own?) had a connection closed mid-response. It says uri = /v1/chat/completions — that's the CLI process talking to the mock server... but the exception appeared in the TEST's isolate log with `dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage`. Actually in dart test output, an unhandled exception in the CLI subprocess wouldn't print that way; this looks like an unhandled async error in the test process itself.     fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —

Author: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit <vabhzw17eg2qu4m9@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Oct 10 15:41:43 2026 +0300

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.

      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —

    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.

      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).

      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the

messages.preview: The failure is an unhandled `HttpException` — likely a lingering in-flight request hitting a torn-down mock server. Let me check the mock server and harness, plus whether main has related fixes:

blocks.text:
The test failed with `HttpException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri = /v1/chat/completions`. This happened asynchronously (`dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage`) — an unhandled async error from an in-flight mock-server request when the server was stopped (or connection torn down) mid-response. Since the failure surfaces as the test failing with that exception, it likely propagated through the test zone.

Where does this come from? The mock server (package:fa_llm_mock) serves the parent + child turns. The error "Connection closed while receiving data" means: client (the CLI's http client, or the harness's own?) had a connection closed mid-response. It says uri = /v1/chat/completions — that's the CLI process talking to the mock server... but the exception appeared in the TEST's isolate log with `dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage`. Actually in dart test output, an unhandled exception in the CLI subprocess wouldn't print that way; this looks like an unhandled async error in the test process itself. Does the harness make HTTP calls? Or the MockLlmServer's client? Hmm, the MockLlmServer is a server. But maybe there's also a health check or the harness sends something.

Wait — actually the traceback only shows `dart:isolate  _RawReceivePort._handleMessage` — a microtask with no useful frames. This is the classic signature of an unhandled error from an HttpClient in the test isolate. Who in the test isolate creates HttpClient requests to /v1/chat/completions? Possibly `harness.startListening()` or waitForScreen doesn't. The CLI runs as a subprocess... unless FA_BIN points to AOT binary (in CI it does) — still a subprocess.

Hmm — maybe the exception came from the mock server handling: the server uses HttpServer; when the CLI process was killed/torn down at test end... but the failure occurred at 07:51:35, mid-run, and the test group started earlier. The test process failed while the test was running.

Alternatively the error was reported by package:test as the test's async error via the harness's stderr listener — harness.startListening() listens to the CLI's output; if the CLI printed an unhandled exception stack... but the frames would be from the CLI.

Actually — in CI this shard runs with FA_BIN=AOT binary; the CLI subprocess's unhandled exceptions are printed to its stderr, and the harness may surface stderr as a test failure. The two-line trace `HttpException ... dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage` is exactly what a Dart AOT binary prints for an unhandled async error (AOT stacks are often truncated to one frame). So: the CLI process itself hit an unhandled HttpException — an LLM client request in the CLI (or a background subagent turn in the CLI) got "Connection closed while receiving data" from the mock server, and it was UNHANDLED, crashing/failing the test.

Where in lib/ would an HttpException be unhandled? The background subagent ("boardwatch") makes its own LLM request. When the test ends (harness.close() kills the CLI?) — but the failure was mid-suite at 07:51:35, and the test was still running...     nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —

    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —

blocks.text:
Neither main nor the PR touched subagent_board_pty_test.dart or lib/src. So the failing test is untouched by both sides — it's a flake (mock HTTP server closed the connection mid-request — a known flake class; this repo has a quarantine system exactly for this, and a `gh-1528 FLAKE` commit fixing an identical class: `Connection reset / closed` in another test).

Per TDD rules and the quarantine convention: a file-level quarantine entry requires >=2 distinct SHAs of red runs and a flake tracker issue. I have ONE red run one SHA. The rule from the harness: "red yields the slot — after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head." The fix path here: pushing the merge-resolution commit creates a NEW head, which re-runs validation CI. The flake may or may not recur.

Options:
1. Just resolve conflicts + push; the new head re-runs CI; if the flake recurs, quarantine.
2. Investigate the test for a real robustness bug and fix it (TDD: reproduce → fix).

Let me look at the failing test to understand the `Connection closed while receiving data` error. The mock server at 127.0.0.1:PORT/v1 — the test spawns a background task that calls the LLM (mock).     nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.

      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:

blocks.text:
The test failed with `HttpException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri = /v1/chat/completions`. This happened asynchronously (`dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage`) — an unhandled async error from an in-flight mock-server request when the server was stopped (or connection torn down) mid-response. Since the failure surfaces as the test failing with that exception, it likely propagated through the test zone.

Where does this come from? The mock server (package:fa_llm_mock) serves the parent + child turns. The error "Connection closed while receiving data" means: client (the CLI's http client, or the harness's own?) had a connection closed mid-response. It says uri = /v1/chat/completions — that's the CLI process talking to the mock server... but the exception appeared in the TEST's isolate log with `dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage`. Actually in dart test output, an unhandled exception in the CLI subprocess wouldn't print that way; this looks like an unhandled async error in the test process itself. Does the harness make HTTP calls? Or the MockLlmServer's client? Hmm, the MockLlmServer is a server. But maybe there's also a health check or the harness sends something.

Wait — actually the traceback only shows `dart:isolate  _RawReceivePort._handleMessage` — a microtask with no useful frames. This is the classic signature of an unhandled error from an HttpClient in the test isolate. Who in the test isolate creates HttpClient requests to /v1/chat/completions? Possibly `harness.startListening()` or waitForScreen doesn't. The CLI runs as a subprocess... unless FA_BIN points to AOT binary (in CI it does) — still a subprocess.

Hmm — maybe the exception came from the mock server handling: the server uses HttpServer; when the CLI process was killed/torn down at test end... but the failure occurred at 07:51:35, mid-run, and the test group started earlier. The test process failed while the test was running.

Alternatively the error was reported by package:test as the test's async error via the harness's stderr listener — harness.startListening() listens to the CLI's output; if the CLI printed an unhandled exception stack... but the frames would be from the CLI.

Actually — in CI this shard runs with FA_BIN=AOT binary; the CLI subprocess's unhandled exceptions are printed to its stderr, and the harness may surface stderr as a test failure. The two-line trace `HttpException ... dart:isolate _RawReceivePort._handleMessage` is exactly what a Dart AOT binary prints for an unhandled async error (AOT stacks are often truncated to one frame). So: the CLI process itself hit an unhandled HttpException — an LLM client request in the CLI (or a background subagent turn in the CLI) got "Connection closed while receiving data" from the mock server, and it was UNHANDLED, crashing/failing the test.

Where in lib/ would an HttpException be unhandled? The background subagent ("boardwatch") makes its own LLM request. B. Move the stamped rehearsal into the pre-merge gate: add the version-stamp arg to ci.yml's PR dry-run step. The nightly step computed `next` from the latest tag. For the PR gate, stamping with a computed next version + running `stamp_staged_release.sh` + dry-run would preserve gh-1522's coverage pre-merge. But that changes ci.yml functional behavior beyond gh-1538's scope — though it resolves the contradiction in the direction both cards want (gh-1538: single pre-merge gate; gh-1522: stamp rehearsal must surface pre-tag).

Option B is the correct engineering resolution: port the gh-1522 stamped dry-run rehearsal into ci.yml's existing publish dry-run step, and retarget the test to ci.yml. The test name: "nightly dry-run rehearses the tag-stamped stage" → "the pre-merge publish dry-run rehearses the tag-stamped stage (gh-1538: moved from the retired nightly full-quality leg)".

Simply dropping the assertion (option A) is the smallest change, but regresses gh-1522's guard, and PR #1526 (gh-1522) explicitly added this rehearsal with tests — removing it would likely fail review again.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
# `|| true`: a stage whose pubspec dropped the version line must reach the
# loud invariant message below, not die silently on grep's exit 1 under
# `set -e` (PR #1526 rework behavioral test).
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the

commit d1b54ef01aaf485acc18c753051db43e3ddad645
Author: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit <vabhzw17eg2qu4m9@gmail.com>

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
# `|| true`: a stage whose pubspec dropped the version line must reach the
# loud invariant message below, not die silently on grep's exit 1 under
# `set -e` (PR #1526 rework behavioral test).
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#

# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
# `|| true`: a stage whose pubspec dropped the version line must reach the
# loud invariant message below, not die silently on grep's exit 1 under
# `set -e` (PR #1526 rework behavioral test).
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc

      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.

Author: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit <vabhzw17eg2qu4m9@gmail.com>

    fix(1385): steering PTY flake — tolerate client aborts in MockLlmServer + phase-0 budget
    
    The two 2026-10-07 shard reds (runs 37624414995, 37562422053) share one
    nondeterminism, not two:
    
    Red 2 (mechanically proven): the steering PTY test's hardKill races the
    soft-yield turn it just triggered — steer -> yieldSource.cancel -> the
    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.
    
    Red 1: phase 0's 60s wait is shorter than the CLI's own 180s connect
    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.
    
    - MockLlmServer: serve through a guarded dispatch that tolerates the
      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.
    
    No product-code defect: both mechanisms are test-infrastructure
    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
    reviewed here against the issue JSON, untouched (contested file).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1522: stamp the staged publish tree with the release version — the git
# tag is the single source of truth, the repo files carry a placeholder
# (0.0.0-dev) and are NEVER mutated by a release.
#
# Usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>
#   <stage-dir> — the staged package tree (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh)
#   <version>   — the release version WITHOUT the leading v (1.0.550)
#
# What it stamps, in order:
#   1. pubspec.yaml `version:` in the stage — and a hard guard that the
#      staged version now EQUALS <version> (a tag/file desync fails here,
#      BEFORE the upload, never mid-publish);
#   2. CHANGELOG.md in the stage — the tag's section is generated and
#      PREPENDED (the repo file keeps its curated `## Unreleased` window;
#      pub.dev's 262144-byte cap is enforced on the STAGED file, which is
#      trimmed of its oldest sections if needed — the repo file stays
#      lossless in git, the archive tail lives in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md).
set -euo pipefail

stage="${1:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
version="${2:?usage: stamp_staged_release.sh <stage-dir> <version>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

pubspec="$stage/pubspec.yaml"
changelog="$stage/CHANGELOG.md"
[ -f "$pubspec" ] || { echo "::error::staged pubspec missing: $pubspec"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$changelog" ] || { echo "::error::staged CHANGELOG missing: $changelog"; exit 1; }

# ── 1. Stamp the version ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"

# Guard (gh-1522 AC: staged version MUST equal the tag name, v1.0.550 →
# 1.0.550) — the stamp above makes this self-evident, but the check is the
# invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
# version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
# here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
# `|| true`: a stage whose pubspec dropped the version line must reach the
# loud invariant message below, not die silently on grep's exit 1 under
# `set -e` (PR #1526 rework behavioral test).
stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)
if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
  echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "staged pubspec stamped to $version"

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the

      # stamps the staged publish tree from it. A hand-bumped version in
      # either pubspec is a mistake now: it desyncs the tag↔staged-file

    bash job hands back at once -> step boundary -> the next /chat/completions
    request fires within milliseconds of the Ctrl+S. When the SIGKILL lands
    mid-request-send, the mock server's parser is mid-body at EOF;
    _HttpParser._onDone raises HttpException('Connection closed while
    receiving data') and _HttpIncoming.listen rethrows it with the
    request-line path (uri = /v1/chat/completions — the exact red-run
    signature). server.listen(mock._handle) had no error handling, so the
    abort escaped as an UNHANDLED ZONE ERROR in the test isolate, which dart
    test attributes to whichever test is active.

    watchdog, so any transient first-request dispatch stall (spinner alive
    at 59s, zero provider bytes) can only be reported, never outlived.

      client-abort classes (HttpException/SocketException — dart:io's
      dead-peer shapes for the read and write legs) and counts them
      (abortedRequests). Served behavior is byte-identical for live
      clients; the scripted queue stays aligned (an aborted request never
      reaches _nextEntry, so nothing is popped).
    - Two regression tests drive both abort windows deterministically
      (data-then-FIN keeps the mid-body parse exact; orderly close keeps
      the dispatch pop exact).
    - steering_persistence_pty_test: phase 0 waits 120s (still far under
      the test's own 10-minute ceiling) and dumps server.chatCalls on
      timeout — 0 means the request never dispatched, >=1 means the
      response pipeline stalled.

    determinism. Quarantine entry for this test is already on main (bot) —
